provenance: Elite five-panel forensic C->Rust porting audit (2026-06): each panel read both the admitted GnuCOBOL 3.2 C (research/gnucobol-3.2/) and the Rust port (crates/gnucobol-rs/src/) for SPECIFIC, code-cited divergences. Panels: (A) memory/ABI/undefined-behavior; (B) numeric/float/decimal; (C) OS/files/linking/concurrency; (D) locale/encoding/i18n; (E) build/dialect/exception/CLI. This is a committed snapshot; GAP-ANALYSIS.md is generated from it and freshness-gated. Each gap is a diff: what the C does, what the port does, the precise divergence, whether it is observable in byte output, severity, and the evidence/plan to close or admit it.
doctrine: A gap is not a defect. The port models OBSERVABLE byte behavior on the pinned x86-64 / C.UTF-8 oracle, not C struct layout, and declares every OS-mutating leaf (dlopen, sigaction, exit, system, fcntl, BDB) a boundary. Many gaps are faithful-under-oracle (diverge only off the pinned locale/build) or admitted-UB (the C is undefined). Severity 'latent' = no oracle-observable divergence today; 'conditional' observable = diverges only under a stated trigger. Nothing is silently omitted: a faithful no-op and an unreproduced abort are both recorded.

gaps.c: common.c:3712/3763 cob_real_get_sign/put_sign branch on COB_MODULE_PTR->ebcdic_sign, using cob_get/put_sign_ebcdic (common.c:1640-1686) when set.

gaps.title: cob_decimal_to_fp_dec64/128 call to_i128().unwrap_or(0) on the unreduced mpz

In-range (<=38-digit) values are a no-op (FLOAT sweep 1476/0 unchanged). >38-digit is unreachable via cobc COMPUTE (38-digit intermediate cap) so there is no direct byte-oracle; test ieee128dec_over_38_digits_reduces_not_zero round-trips a 40-digit value through the FLOAT.1-sealed dec128_decode and asserts it equals the top-34-digit truncation (non-zero).

gaps.title: DIVIDE intermediate precision capped at i128 (~38 digits) vs GMP 38-digit-shifted dividend
gaps.c: numeric.c:2259 cob_decimal_div does shift_decimal(d1, COB_MAX_DIGITS=38 + |neg scale|) then mpz_tdiv_q: the GMP dividend routinely reaches 70-90+ digits at full precision.
gaps.rust: arith.rs:176 compute_divide computes a.mag.checked_mul(pow10(k)) in i128 then num/b.mag; i128 holds ~38 digits so large k overflows -> ArithError::OutOfRange.
gaps.diff: C produces a correct truncated quotient when the scaled dividend exceeds 38 digits; Rust fails closed. Rust also uses only result_scale(+1) guard digits, not the full 38 guard, so the truncated last digit can differ on non-terminating quotients.
gaps.observable: conditional: dividend*10^(result_scale-a.scale+b.scale) exceeds ~1.7e38 (high-precision/chained COMPUTE division)
gaps.plan: FIXED (gnucobol-rs 0.7.85, in-place): compute_divide keeps the proven i128 fast path but falls back to an arbitrary-precision Mpz divide (divide_via_mpz: Mpz tdiv_qr, quotient + sticky remainder) the moment the i128 dividend/divisor scaling overflows -- mirroring GnuCOBOL's GMP shift to COB_MAX_DIGITS (numeric.c:2260) so it never fails closed. Sealed divide_sweep 736/0 + round_sweep 6720/0 unchanged (in-range hits the i128 path). Oracle-proven: DIVIDE 2 BY 3 into a PIC 9V9(37) receiver (the 2*10^38 intermediate overflows i128) -> 0.(37 sixes) trunc / 0.(36 sixes)7 ROUNDED, matching the built GnuCOBOL oracle. Test divide_intermediate_over_i128_vs_cobc.

gaps.title: ADD/SUBTRACT operand alignment overflows i128 where GMP is exact
gaps.c: numeric.c:2181 cob_decimal_add/sub align via shift_decimal in GMP -- upshifted operand and sum are arbitrary precision.
gaps.rust: arith.rs:141 upscale does mag.checked_mul(pow10(n)) + checked_add, all i128 -> OutOfRange on overflow.
gaps.diff: Adding operands with very different scales (18-digit integer + 18-fractional) upshifts past 38 digits and overflows i128; C computes the exact aligned sum and narrows only at store.
gaps.observable: conditional: max(scale)+integer-digits of an operand exceeds 38 during alignment

In-range is the i128 fast path (cob_decimal arith sweep 5400/0 unchanged). Oracle-proven: ADD 1.5 TO A=2e20 (PIC 9(21)) -- aligning A to scale 18 needs 2e38 > i128 -- yields 200000000000000000001, matching the built GnuCOBOL oracle. Test add_intermediate_over_i128_vs_cobc.

gaps.c: numeric.c:1184 cob_decimal_set_packed accumulates val=val*100+pack_to_bin[byte] using the 256-entry table (numeric.c:125): invalid nibbles fold with a carry (e.g. byte 0x1A->20).

Valid BCD is unchanged (packed_arith 1800/0, numcmp 1024/0, cob_decimal 5400/0); invalid nibble oracle-proven: PIC S9(3) COMP-3 = X"2F6C", COMPUTE acc = P3 + 0 -> 256 via cobc (PACK_TO_BIN[0x2F]=25), where the old nibble split gave 356. Test packed_invalid_nibble_arith_vs_cobc.

gaps.title: Mpf::get_str rounds half-up; GMP mpf_get_str rounds half-to-even at digit 96
gaps.c: numeric.c:864 mpf_get_str(...,96,...); GMP rounds to nearest, ties-to-even on the exact binary value.
gaps.rust: mpf.rs:423 get_str uses round_up = d[ndigits]>=5 (round-half-up).

So mpf.rs:423 (round_up = d[ndigits] >= 5) already matches GMP exactly. Recorded as a verified non-divergence with the oracle.
